analyst_view.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points, unbeaten at home) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points); Werder have won eight of the last nine top-flight meetings at the Weserstadion, and Fuellkrug leads the league with nine goals, six from set pieces. Werder's creator Marco Gruell (calf; two goals and eight assists) is the big doubt: he went off at Stuttgart with a long-standing calf problem (90min, 8 Nov), last night's report had Thioune saying he had not trained, though the Bundesliga's predicted XI still lists him; Weiser (thigh) is out and counted. Hamburg are without Remberg, Nadir, Torunarigha, Sambi Lokonga and captain Poulsen (the numbers count Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga for goals), with Daka and Muheim, who has three long-range goals, in the predicted XI. Florian Badstuebner referees: his low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already taking about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga, and 4% off Werder for Weiser. They do not count Gruell, Werder's main creator, who is a real doubt with his calf; sources disagree on whether he starts, so I go 4% lower, to about 2.6 (was -6), with Fuellkrug's set pieces still a threat.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Werder expected to win most of them at home against Hamburg's back three with wing-backs. With or without Gruell, Werder's wide play and Fuellkrug's set-piece threat drive their corners, which the numbers see, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstuebner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game, and both sides have been booked less than usual lately (counted). Thioune and Polzin are old colleagues and nothing in the news points to extra needle beyond the derby itself, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%), much of it built through Gruell. With him doubtful and Weiser out on the right, Werder may lose two of their main suppliers, so I take 2% off, to about 30.6 (was -3, now that his absence is less certain).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six games already added (+15%). If Gruell, who has set up eight goals, misses out, Werder's chances should be fewer and less clean; as he is only doubtful, I take 3% off, to about 10.5 (was -4).
